tax.text: He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill and praised its tax cuts for families.
tax.quote: The One Big Beautiful Bill delivers the largest tax cuts for families in a generation.

wages.text: He voted against the Raise the Wage Act, which passed the House in 2019.

trade.text: He praised the 2025 tariffs as a way to protect American workers and businesses.
trade.quote: the United States will see fair trade as President Trump announced tariffs that level the playing field for American workers and businesses.

schools.text: He endorsed expanding school choice and supported a federal tax credit for K–12 scholarships.
schools.quote: School choice works when parents are trusted, students have options, and classrooms focus on learning.

safety.text: He introduced a bill to let law enforcement officers and trained civilians carry firearms in school zones.
safety.quote: Would allow for retired law enforcement officers authorized under federal law to carry firearms to do so in a school zone

immigration.text: He supported bills to strengthen ICE authority and increase penalties for deported felons who return illegally.
immigration.quote: Kate’s Law establishes that deported felons who return to the U.S. see enhanced penalties upon returning illegally.

guns.text: He voted against the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and opposed its new restrictions on gun ownership.
guns.quote: you don’t restrict law-abiding citizens from protecting themselves with the weapons of their choice

abortion.text: He voted against bills expanding abortion access and said he would continue to oppose them.
abortion.quote: Today, I voted against House Democrats' "Abortion on Demand Until Birth Act" and "Ensuring Access to Abortion Act."

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He supported legislation requiring sex in school athletics to be defined by reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
gender.quote: sex shall be recognized based solely on a person's reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

cannabis.text: He voted No on final passage of the MORE Act.
cannabis.quote: Vote Question: On Passage MORE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay

health.text: He called for dismantling and defunding the Affordable Care Act, saying government should not control the health care system.
health.quote: The government has no business controlling the healthcare system.

energy.text: He supported expanding domestic energy production and opposed restrictions he said could raise costs and threaten jobs.
energy.quote: I will continue to fight against this ban and urge the President to reverse course

voting.text: He supported requiring proof of citizenship to register, photo ID to vote, and stronger voter-roll checks.
voting.quote: Requiring proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections.

trade.text: He said he would roll back tariffs because they have raised prices.
trade.quote: To build affordability in this economy, we need policy that will roll back tariffs which have raised prices

housing.text: He called for clearing barriers to build more affordable housing.
housing.quote: prices, clearing barriers to build more affordable housing.

schools.text: He supports investing in teachers and classrooms and says a strong public education system builds future leaders.
schools.quote: A strong public education system builds the next generation of leaders.

safety.text: He supports law enforcement as well as mental health support and opportunity as parts of community safety.
safety.quote: I support law enforcement, and I believe true safety requires stability, mental health support, and opportunity.

immigration.text: He criticized mass deportation and said he would pursue humane immigration reform.
immigration.quote: The homeland security budget for ICE is $70 Billion dealing with mass deportation. It has resulted in major uproars in our cities and has led to loss of human life. I would push for Immigration reform that is humane in our present environment.
